title: Past continuous 2
note: Questions, negatives and the when/while contrast above a2_past_continuous. C57 2026-09-04 (James smoke): card 1 is a recap of Past continuous 1. Correcting this note's old claim that a2_past_continuous 'did in-progress and background only' - it also has a Questions card and a Negative card, including 'Not Did you working?'. So questions and negatives here are REVISION at a harder level; the genuinely new material is while vs when and two simultaneous long actions. C33: the usual job is an interrupted action - was -ing WHEN + past simple - not clock-time snapshots. Czech trap: no auxiliary in the question (*What you did doing), and while/when both render kdyz. James smoke 2026-09-04: A0 - while and when are BOTH correct before a long action, so items 4 and 15 accept both and no longer list When as a Quiz distractor; two forced items added where the choice is real (when + short action). Two gap answers duplicated their own stem (Were you waiting still waiting). Negative item rebuilt - she wasn't studying when her friends arrived was not a thing anyone says; James picked 'when I phoned her', changed to 'when I saw her' because F3 fires on phoned (phone is taught as a noun before this slot, not as a verb). Use `wrong` sentences moved to form errors: a ringing phone and starting rain both have duration, so while + them is arguable, and B1 bans an arguable error.

cards.title: Past continuous 2
points: You already know **was / were** + **-ing** for the long action.
The question and the negative come back **harder** here — and **while** is new.

rows: **While** I was cooking, my phone rang.

examples.en: **What were** you doing at eight o'clock?
examples.cz: Co jsi dělal v osm hodin?

cards.title: You already know
points: **was / were** + **-ing** = an action **in progress** at a past time.
Its usual job: the long action is **cut** by a short one.
Questions and negatives came in **Past continuous 1** too — here they get harder.

examples.en: She **was cooking when** I came home.

cards.title: Questions
points: **was /** were comes before the subject. There is no **did** in this question.

cards.title: while and when
points: Czech **když** covers both. The choice depends on the action that follows.

rows: **While** I was cooking, my phone rang.
I was cooking **when** my phone rang.
**While** I was reading, my sister was cooking.
~~While my phone rang, I was cooking.~~
**While** I was cooking, my phone rang.

items.en: What were you doing at eight o'clock?
items.cz: Co jsi dělal v osm hodin?
items.gap: What ____ at eight o'clock? (you / do)
accepts: What were you doing at eight o'clock?
items.wrong: What you were doing at eight o'clock?
items.explanation: Question order: **were** + you + doing. No **did** with a continuous form.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek v otázce: **were** + you + doing. S průběhovým tvarem se **did** nepoužívá.

items.en: Was he working when you arrived?
items.cz: Pracoval, když jsi přišel?
items.gap: ____ when you arrived? (he / work)
accepts: Was he working when you arrived?
items.wrong: Did he working when you arrived?
items.explanation: **he** takes **was**: Was he working. The arriving is the short action.
items.explanation_cz: **he** má **was**: Was he working. Příchod je ta krátká akce.

items.en: I wasn't sleeping when you called.
items.cz: Nespal jsem, když jsi volal.
items.gap: I ____ when you called. (not / sleep)
accepts: I wasn't sleeping when you called.
I was not sleeping when you called.
items.wrong: I didn't sleeping when you called.
items.explanation: Negative: **wasn't** + sleeping. The call interrupted the sleeping.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor: **wasn't** + sleeping. Hovor přerušil spaní.

items.en: They weren't listening while I was talking.
items.cz: Neposlouchali, když jsem mluvil.
items.gap: They ____ while I was talking. (not / listen)
accepts: They weren't listening while I was talking.
They were not listening while I was talking.
items.explanation: Two long actions running together, so both take **was /** were + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě dlouhé akce běží zároveň, takže obě mají **was /** were + -ing.
items.wrong: They didn't listening while I was talking.

items.en: While I was cooking, my phone rang.
items.cz: Zatímco jsem vařil, zazvonil mi telefon.
items.gap: ____ I was cooking, my phone rang. (while / when)
accepts: While I was cooking, my phone rang.
When I was cooking, my phone rang.
items.wrong: While I was cook, my phone rang.
items.explanation: **While** or **when** both work in front of the long action; **while** is the clearer one. Only **when** works in front of a short action.
items.explanation_cz: Před dlouhou akcí jde **while** i **when**; **while** je jasnější. Před krátkou akcí jde jen **when**.

items.en: I was reading when she came home.
items.cz: Četl jsem, když přišla domů.
items.gap: I was reading ____ she came home. (while / when)
accepts: I was reading when she came home.
items.wrong: I was reading while she came home.
items.explanation: **when** introduces the short action that cuts in: she came home.
items.explanation_cz: **when** uvádí krátkou akci, která přeruší: přišla domů.

items.en: What was she wearing?
items.cz: Co měla na sobě?
items.gap: What ____? (she / wear)
accepts: What was she wearing?
items.explanation: **she** takes **was**: What was she wearing.
items.explanation_cz: **she** má **was**: What was she wearing.

items.en: Were you still waiting when I called?
items.cz: Čekal jsi ještě, když jsem volal?
items.gap: ____ when I called? (you / still / wait)
accepts: Were you still waiting when I called?
items.explanation: **you** takes **were**: Were you waiting. The call cut into the waiting.
items.explanation_cz: **you** má **were**: Were you waiting. Hovor přerušil čekání.
items.wrong: Was you still waiting when I called?

items.en: It wasn't raining when we left.
items.cz: Nepršelo, když jsme odcházeli.
items.gap: It ____ when we left. (not / rain)
accepts: It wasn't raining when we left.
It was not raining when we left.
items.explanation: **it** takes **wasn't** + raining. Leaving is the short action.
items.explanation_cz: **it** má **wasn't** + raining. Odchod je ta krátká akce.

items.en: While she was driving, she saw the accident.
items.cz: Zatímco řídila, viděla tu nehodu.
items.gap: ____ she was driving, she saw the accident. (while / when)
accepts: While she was driving, she saw the accident.
items.explanation: **While** goes with the long action, the driving.
items.explanation_cz: **While** patří k dlouhé akci, k řízení.

items.en: Why were they laughing?
items.cz: Proč se smáli?
items.gap: Why ____? (they / laugh)
accepts: Why were they laughing?
items.explanation: **they** takes **were**: Why were they laughing.
items.explanation_cz: **they** má **were**: Why were they laughing.

items.en: We weren't working when our boss came in.
items.cz: Nepracovali jsme, když přišel náš šéf.
items.gap: We ____ when our boss came in. (not / work)
accepts: We weren't working when our boss came in.
We were not working when our boss came in.
items.explanation: **we** takes **weren't** + working.
items.explanation_cz: **we** má **weren't** + working.
items.wrong: We didn't working when our boss came in.

items.en: Where were you going when I saw you?
items.cz: Kam jsi šel, když jsem tě viděl?
items.gap: Where ____ when I saw you? (you / go)
accepts: Where were you going when I saw you?
items.wrong: Where you were going when I saw you?
items.explanation: After the question word the order is **were** + you + going. The subject comes second.
items.explanation_cz: Po tázacím slově je pořadí **were** + you + going. Podmět je až druhý.

items.en: Who were you talking to when I came in?
items.cz: S kým jsi mluvil, když jsem přišel?
items.gap: Who ____ to when I came in? (you / talk)
accepts: Who were you talking to when I came in?
items.wrong: Who did you talking to when I came in?
items.explanation: **did** never stands with a **-ing** form. The question is **were** you talking.
items.explanation_cz: **did** nikdy nestojí s tvarem na **-ing**. Otázka je **were** you talking.

items.en: She wasn't working when I saw her.
items.cz: Nepracovala, když jsem ji viděl.
items.gap: She ____ when I saw her. (not / work)
accepts: She wasn't working when I saw her.
She was not working when I saw her.
items.wrong: She didn't working when I saw her.
items.explanation: Negative: **wasn't** + working. Seeing her is the short action.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor: **wasn't** + working. To, že jsem ji viděl, je krátká akce.

items.en: While we were waiting, it started to rain.
items.cz: Zatímco jsme čekali, začalo pršet.
items.gap: ____ we were waiting, it started to rain. (while / when)
accepts: While we were waiting, it started to rain.
When we were waiting, it started to rain.
items.wrong: While we waiting, it started to rain.
items.explanation: **While** or **when** both work in front of the long action — the waiting. **While** is the clearer one.
items.explanation_cz: Před dlouhou akcí — před čekáním — jde **while** i **when**. **While** je jasnější.

items.en: Were they still working at six?
items.cz: Pracovali ještě v šest?
items.gap: ____ at six? (they / still / work)
accepts: Were they still working at six?
items.wrong: Was they still working at six?
items.explanation: **they** takes **were**: Were they working. *still* says the work was in progress.
items.explanation_cz: **they** má **were**: Were they working. *still* říká, že práce probíhala.

items.en: What were your children doing when you got home?
items.cz: Co dělaly tvoje děti, když jsi přišel domů?
items.gap: What ____ when you got home? (your children / do)
accepts: What were your children doing when you got home?
items.wrong: What was your children doing when you got home?
items.explanation: **children** is plural, so the question takes **were**, not was.
items.explanation_cz: **children** je množné číslo, takže otázka má **were**, ne was.

items.en: They weren't playing football because it was raining.
items.cz: Nehráli fotbal, protože pršelo.
items.gap: They ____ football because it was raining. (not / play)
accepts: They weren't playing football because it was raining.
They were not playing football because it was raining.
items.wrong: They didn't playing football because it was raining.
items.explanation: **they** takes **weren't** + playing. The rain is the background that was going on.
items.explanation_cz: **they** má **weren't** + playing. Déšť je pozadí, které zrovna probíhalo.

items.en: He was walking home when he met an old friend.
items.cz: Šel domů, když potkal starého kamaráda.
items.gap: He ____ home when he met an old friend. (walk)
accepts: He was walking home when he met an old friend.
items.wrong: He was walking home when he meet an old friend.
items.explanation: The walk is the long action: **was walking**. Meeting the friend cuts into it, so it is past simple.
items.explanation_cz: Cesta domů je dlouhá akce: **was walking**. Setkání ji přeruší, proto minulý čas prostý.

items.en: They were living in Brno when we visited them.
items.cz: Bydleli v Brně, když jsme je navštívili.
items.gap: They ____ in Brno when we visited them. (live)
accepts: They were living in Brno when we visited them.
items.wrong: They was living in Brno when we visited them.
items.explanation: **they** takes **were** + living — the years in Brno are the background to the visit.
items.explanation_cz: **they** má **were** + living — roky v Brně jsou pozadí k návštěvě.

items.en: While I was reading, my sister was cooking dinner.
items.cz: Zatímco jsem četl, sestra vařila večeři.
items.gap: While I was reading, my sister ____ dinner. (cook)
accepts: While I was reading, my sister was cooking dinner.
items.explanation: Two long actions running side by side: **while** + both in **was /** were + -ing.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě dlouhé akce běží vedle sebe: **while** a obě ve tvaru **was /** were + -ing.

items.en: Was he driving to work when you called?
items.cz: Jel do práce, když jsi volal?
items.gap: ____ to work when you called? (he / drive)
accepts: Was he driving to work when you called?
items.wrong: Did he driving to work when you called?
items.explanation: **he** takes **was**: Was he driving. **did** cannot stand with a -ing form.
items.explanation_cz: **he** má **was**: Was he driving. **did** nemůže stát s -ing tvarem.

items.en: What were you doing when the film started?
items.cz: Co jsi dělal, když ten film začal?
items.gap: What ____ when the film started? (you / do)
accepts: What were you doing when the film started?
items.wrong: What did you doing when the film started?
items.explanation: **did** never meets a -ing form. The long action takes **were** you doing.
items.explanation_cz: **did** se s -ing tvarem nepotkává. Dlouhá akce má **were** you doing.

items.en: She was working in Prague when we met her.
items.cz: Pracovala v Praze, když jsme ji potkali.
items.gap: She ____ in Prague when we met her. (work)
accepts: She was working in Prague when we met her.
items.wrong: She were working in Prague when we met her.
items.explanation: **she** takes **was** + working. The job was going on when the meeting cut in.
items.explanation_cz: **she** má **was** + working. Práce probíhala, když do ní vstoupilo setkání.

items.en: We were still eating when they arrived.
items.cz: Ještě jsme jedli, když přišli.
items.gap: We ____ when they arrived. (still / eat)
accepts: We were still eating when they arrived.
items.wrong: We was still eating when they arrived.
items.explanation: **we** takes **were**, and *still* puts the meal in progress: **were still eating**.
items.explanation_cz: **we** má **were** a *still* říká, že jídlo probíhalo: **were still eating**.

items.en: I was walking home when I met my old teacher.
items.cz: Šel jsem domů, když jsem potkal svého starého učitele.
items.gap: I was walking home ____ I met my old teacher. (when / while)
accepts: I was walking home when I met my old teacher.
items.wrong: I was walking home while I met my old teacher.
items.explanation: Meeting someone takes a moment, so only **when** fits. **While** needs the long action.
items.explanation_cz: Potkat někoho je okamžik, proto jde jen **when**. **While** patří k dlouhé akci.

items.en: We were waiting when the bus arrived.
items.cz: Čekali jsme, když přijel ten autobus.
items.gap: We were waiting ____ the bus arrived. (when / while)
accepts: We were waiting when the bus arrived.
items.wrong: We were waiting while the bus arrived.
items.explanation: Arriving is the short action, so it takes **when**. The waiting is the long one.
items.explanation_cz: Příjezd je krátká akce, proto **when**. Čekání je ta dlouhá.
